register_world_behavior_for_multiple_bui.sql: INSERT OR IGNORE INTO m6_world_builds(world_id, build_name) VALUES(?, ?)
register_world_behavior_for_multiple_bui.semantics: UNION/accumulate — adds (world_id, build_name) pairs; INSERT OR IGNORE means a repeat pair is a no-op. It does NOT replace, delete, or overwrite prior builds for that world_id.
call_sequence_register_world_1_build_A_t: final state of world 1: references BOTH build_A AND build_B (coexist, NOT replace)
register_world_behavior_for_multiple_bui.supports_multiple_distinct_worlds: YES at the API level — world_id is a free int parameter and the table is a many-to-many map. NO in production — the sole caller (m6_production_indexing.py:83) always passes 1, so every indexed build lands in the same World 1.
register_world_behavior_for_multiple_bui.note: Builds accumulate into World 1. The World->Builds cardinality is 1->N (one World referencing many builds), never 1->1 per build. There is no path that gives each indexed build its own distinct World.

build_query_isolation_detail.production_wiring: authority.py:450 build_name = resolve_build_name(store, project_root); authority.py:453 result = m6_fn(store, build_name, *args, **kwargs) — every M6 query (lookup_symbol, search_code, find_callers, find_references, get_symbol_context, get_class_members, search_bodies, get_file_map, get_source) is scoped to that ONE build_name
build_query_isolation_detail.consequence: even when distinct build_names coexist in World 1 (Scenario B), only the first-inserted build is reachable through the production read path. Every other indexed build is INVISIBLE — there is no API to select it. A re-index that changes insertion order silently shifts which build is queryable.

trace_index_build_A_then_build_B.can_you_query_both: NO. resolve_build_name returns 'default' (the only build). project_build('default') returns the merged union of A's facts + B's disjoint facts, with no way to ask for 'A only' or 'B only'. The two builds are NOT independently queryable.
trace_index_build_A_then_build_B.verdict: broken — silent payload loss on same-canon facts + cross-contamination on disjoint facts + no per-build query path

summary.register_world_behavior_for_multiple_bui: Accumulates builds into a World via INSERT OR IGNORE (union semantics, never replaces). register_world(1,{A}) then register_world(1,{B}) leaves World 1 referencing BOTH A and B. The API supports distinct world_ids, but the sole production caller always passes literal 1, so all builds collapse into one World.
summary.root_cause: M6 production indexing (m6_production_indexing.py:83) hardcodes world_id=1 and ignores the real v2 World-identity derivation (store_v2/world_id.py / worlds.py / snapshot_builds.world_id). Combined with build_name defaulting to 'default' (runner.py:1122) and resolve_build_name (m6_query.py:65-81) returning only the first-inserted build, the M6 path cannot represent, retain, or query more than one build. Same-canon facts across builds silently lose the second writer's payload (m6_store.py:158-166 updates buildset_id only, never payload_json).
